626	def run_http(server: object, settings: Settings, *, kind: str) -> None:
627	    """Build the wrapped HTTP app and serve it via uvicorn.
628	
629	    Honours the project's TLS / mTLS settings: when
630	    ``http_tls_certfile`` + ``http_tls_keyfile`` are set, uvicorn
631	    terminates TLS itself. Adding ``http_tls_ca_certs`` and
632	    flipping ``http_tls_client_cert_required=true`` upgrades the
633	    listener to full mutual TLS — connections without a client cert
634	    signed by a CA in the bundle are refused at the handshake
635	    layer, before any ASGI middleware sees the request.
636	    """
637	    import ssl
638	
639	    import uvicorn
640	
641	    app = build_http_app(server, settings, kind=kind)
642	    tls_kwargs = _uvicorn_tls_kwargs(settings, ssl_module=ssl)
643	    # Windows: async psycopg refuses to run on the ProactorEventLoop and
644	    # needs a SelectorEventLoop. ``__main__`` sets the selector policy at
645	    # startup, but uvicorn's own loop setup reinstalls the *proactor*
646	    # policy on Windows before serving — which silently breaks every
647	    # database connection under the HTTP transport (the connection pool
648	    # times out after 30s and the session crashes). stdio is unaffected;
649	    # nothing overrides the policy there. Re-pin the selector policy and
650	    # tell uvicorn to leave the loop alone (``loop="none"``) so it runs on
651	    # the loop our policy creates. No-op off Windows.
652	    if sys.platform == "win32":
653	        # CPython 3.14 privatized WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy to
654	        # _WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy; fall back to it when the public

657	            getattr(asyncio, "WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy", None) or asyncio._WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy

662	    # large, overloaded ``uvicorn.run`` signature; the dict's contents
663	    # are already constrained by ``_uvicorn_tls_kwargs``.

668	    """Translate the project's TLS settings into the uvicorn keyword arg shape.
669	
670	    ``ssl_module`` is parameterised so tests can pass a stub without
671	    importing the real :mod:`ssl` (avoids creating a real SSL context
672	    just to assert the argument routing). At runtime callers pass
673	    ``ssl`` directly.
674	
675	    Returns an empty dict when TLS isn't configured, so the call site
676	    can ``uvicorn.run(..., **tls_kwargs)`` unconditionally.
677	    """
678	    if settings.http_tls_certfile is None or settings.http_tls_keyfile is None:
679	        return {}
680	    kwargs: dict[str, object] = {
681	        "ssl_certfile": settings.http_tls_certfile,
682	        "ssl_keyfile": settings.http_tls_keyfile,
683	        # Pin to PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER explicitly. On Python 3.10+ this
684	        # carries SSLContext.minimum_version = TLSv1_2 by default, so

Analysis of the diff:

**src/mcpg/__main__.py & src/mcpg/http_runtime.py** — Both add the same Python 3.14 compatibility shim for the Windows event loop policy. The new code path:
- Only executes when `sys.platform == "win32"` at process startup
- Reads a module attribute name (`WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy`) from the stdlib `asyncio` module — not from any attacker-controllable input
- Falls back to the private `_WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy` when the public name is gone in CPython 3.14
- No source→sink data flow; no user input reaches the getattr/attribute lookup

Worst-case failure is a startup AttributeError on a future Python where neither name exists — that's a portability bug, not a security defect.

**pyproject.toml** — Adds `<2` upper bound on `mcp[cli]`. Purely defensive dependency pinning; no runtime impact.

**tests/unit/test_config.py** — Test change to make `/usr/bin`-style strings pass `os.path.isabs` on Windows via `os.path.abspath`. Test-only, no production reachability.

**tests/unit/test_http_runtime.py** — Adds `**kwargs` to a fake uvicorn to swallow the win32-only `loop="none"` kwarg. Test-only.

No entry points, sinks, parsers, allowlists, permissions, IPC, or IaC surfaces are touched. No attacker-influenceable value flows through any changed line.
